audit.whatIsWrong: Three places on the page — whys[4], spikes[2] and the mid paragraph — described GNAR! (R) as 'a point-and-click AoE stun'. It is neither point-and-click nor an unconditional stun.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Mega Gnar throws everything around him in a chosen direction, dealing damage and slowing them. Any enemy that hits a WALL is stunned and takes bonus damage.' It is a directional throw with a chosen vector, and against a target with no wall behind them it is a slow, not a stun. That inverts the advice completely: the counterplay is positional (fight in open lane, keep terrain off your back), not 'dodge the point-and-click'. Cooldown is 90/60/30 — a 90s rank-1 window, not something he has every fight.
audit.corrected: whys[4], spikes[2], mid, tldr, enemyWin, dosFull[0].d and phases[4].why all now state the wall requirement and the directional throw, with the 90s rank-1 number attached.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers published a chart that gave Heimerdinger levels 1, 2, 3 and 6 while the prose beside it said the opposite: whys[0] 'mini-Gnar's boomerang and hop autos out-poke you', whys[1] 'concede CS and stay safe', whys[2] 'genuinely even', whys[4] describes his one flip window. The early paragraph opens 'Level 1 Gnar starts ahead'.
audit.why: Gnar out-ranges a nest-less Heimerdinger at levels 1-2 (Boomerang Throw at 1100 range, no cost), level 3 is even once the second turret and beam contest his approach, Heimerdinger peaks at 4-5 with three charges plus CH-3X, Gnar's only flip is a level-6 Mega transform, and both item stages return to Heimerdinger.
audit.corrected: Both layers flipped to Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Heimerdinger / Gnar / Heimerdinger / Heimerdinger as one atomic paired group, matching the packet and the mirror audit, with ratings re-cut.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5] called Liandry's Torment a moment to 'force fights on GNAR!'s cooldown' and phases[4] claimed 'Upgraded E or W deletes his all-in'.
audit.why: First item is genuinely Heimerdinger's stage here, but for the siege reason — Gnar has to enter the nest to do anything and cannot shred turrets fast enough. Level 6 is Gnar's stage, not a window Heimerdinger's UPGRADE!!! resolves.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and phases[5].why rewritten to the real reasons for each spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer told you to 'track GNAR!' as if it were a short lane cooldown, with no number.
audit.why: GNAR! is 90s at rank 1 and gated behind a full Rage bar, so the real read is the Rage bar and his form, not a timer. Wallop (Mega W) at a flat 7s is the stun he actually has repeatedly.
audit.corrected: tldr and dosFull[0].d now say to read the Rage bar and carry the 90s figure.

notes: The most valuable correction on this page: GNAR! was described as 'a point-and-click AoE stun' in three separate places. Riot's text makes it a directional throw where ONLY enemies who hit a wall are stunned — against a Heimerdinger standing in open lane it is a displacement plus slow. That changes the counterplay from 'dodge it' to 'control which terrain is behind you', which is actionable for an immobile champion with no dash. Both layers also published a chart that contradicted their own prose in six of seven rows (the early paragraph literally opens 'Level 1 Gnar starts ahead' under a chart row reading Heimerdinger 8/10); fixed as one paired atomic group. NOT ASSERTED: whether the CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade stun can interrupt the Rage-transform animation, and whether Mega Gnar's Wallop out-prioritises the grenade when both land in the same tick — neither is answerable from Riot's text.
